Everything below the line is the PR body.

---

## What does this PR do?

- Closes #104

Since PR #85 a host can be away for part of a day. The booking page removed those slots and said nothing,
so an attendee saw a gap with no reason and no "Book with" link. A whole-day entry already shows the
"away" panel with the emoji, the reason, the public note and the redirect. This PR gives a partial-day
entry the same panel, in the place in the day where the window falls. This is "alternative 1" from the
PR #85 design.

**The slot engine.** A partial-day window now stays in the host's `dateRanges`, so its slots are generated
and then marked `away`, the same path a whole day takes. The window is still subtracted from
`oooExcludedDateRanges`, which is what `ensureAvailableUsers` checks a booking against, so an away slot
cannot be booked (criterion 2). The per-day away map (`IOutOfOfficeData`) keeps one record per date and
gains an optional `windows` list on it, each window carrying its UTC `start` and `end` and the entry's
data. A date without `windows` is away all day, as before. A whole-day entry wins over a window on the
same date, and a holiday replaces windows but not a whole-day entry. `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows`
in `date-ranges.ts` reads the stored wall-clock values with the DST-safe parse from PR #85 and lists every
host-zone date a window touches, so a window past midnight appears under both dates.

**Slot marking.** `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` marks a slot on a windowed date away only when the slot
overlaps a window: `slotStart < windowEnd && slotEnd > windowStart`. Any overlap counts (criterion 1), so
a slot that straddles the leave time is away too, which matches what the booking guard rejects. Whole-day
marking is unchanged. The windows are parsed to numbers once per `getSlots` call.

**The booker.** `AvailableTimes` renders one away panel at the first slot of each run of away slots and
hides the away slots, so the panel sits between the slots before and after the window (criterion 3). Two
windows on one day give two panels. The panel keeps today's text; no new string. The "Book with" button
already works from the slot's `toUser`, so the redirect needs only the data (criterion 4).
`AvailableTimeSlots` now hides the time-format toggle only when every slot of the day is away, not when
the first one is. `DatePicker`, `useNonEmptyScheduleDays` and the weekly view already require every slot
to be away before they treat a day as away, so a window that covers the whole working day renders as a
whole-day entry (criterion 5) and nothing else changes for them. API v2 slot responses filter `away` and
are unchanged (criterion 7).

**Decisions, from the issue's open questions.** Any overlap marks a slot away, because the fully-inside
rule would show slots the booking guard then rejects. The panel keeps today's text; its place between the
slots shows the window, and that is also the answer for attendees far from the host's zone. Two windows
give two panels. Criterion 4 stays, shown by a unit test; the redirect switch in the form is still
disabled in this fork, so a hand-edited `OutOfOfficeEntry.toUserId` row is the only way to see it live.

## Design

**Decision.** Keep the away map keyed by date and hang the windows under the date record. Whole days and
partial days then share one map, one lookup in the slot engine and one set of booker readers.

**Alternatives considered.**

1. A separate map of windows next to `datesOutOfOffice`. Every consumer of the map (the slot engine, the
   tRPC slots util, the onboarding hook) would take a second argument, and the whole-day-wins rule would
   live in two places.
2. One record per window with the date record replaced by a list. Every reader of
   `IOutOfOfficeData["anyDate"]` in the booker and the `DatePicker` would change shape for a feature that
   most days never use.
3. Mark only slots fully inside the window. A slot that straddles the leave time would look bookable and
   fail at booking time, a silent error.

**Rationale.** The windowed record is additive: a date without `windows` is exactly what it was before,
so existing tests pass unchanged (criterion 6), and the engine keeps the whole-day and partial-day split
that PR #85 introduced. Windows are read from the same `wallClockToTimeZone` parse, so the DST behaviour
is the one already tested.

**Consequences.** `SlotInfo` in `packages/features/calendars/lib/types.ts` still lists no `notes`, though
the server sends it and the panel shows it; the new booker test widens the type locally and the component
is left alone. `buildDateRanges` now skips windowed dates when it removes whole days from
`oooExcludedDateRanges`; without that line a windowed date lost all of its bookable ranges, which the
new tests caught.

# Issue #<N> -- <issue title>

## Class Diagram

![Class diagram](111-kojoshuay-class.png)

## Sequence Diagram

![Sequence diagram](111-kojoshuay-sequence.png)

## Q&A

**Class diagram:**

1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.

The two most important classes are `SecurityView` and `CachedFeatureRepository` 
* `SecurityView` (new client component) manages the local UI state to intercept clicks, serving as the primary frontend safeguard that forces admins to view a warning dialog before turning off 2FA
* `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide` (new helper module) embodies the core architectural design decision for this feature. It bypasses the cache to read the security state directly from the live database, establishing the foundation so that the upcoming login check never acts on stale data.

2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.

The most important relationship is the separation of database reads and writes. To ensure the security policy, and by extension the admin page, never act on a cached value, the `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide` helper reads directly from the live database (`PrismaFeatureRepository`). However, when an admin saves a change, the `toggleFeatureFlag` endpoint saves through the `CachedFeatureRepository`. This ensures that whenever the setting is updated, the cache is automatically cleared so the rest of the application does not rely on old data.

3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?

No, not as of this moment. 

**Sequence diagram:**

1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?

The sequence starts when the Admin clicks the  toggle switch to 'off' inside the `SecurityView` component. The outcome is that, after the admin confirms in the warning dialog, the database updates the `enabled` field to `false` and records the admin's ID (`updatedBy`). Subsequently, the cache clears its stale keys, and the frontend updates the screen by showing a success toast, refreshing the queries, and flipping the switch to 'off'.

2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.

* The `SecurityView` intercepts the click locally. Instead of immediately firing a network request, it halts the process to display a warning dialog, requiring confirmation from the admin (new code).
* Once the network request hits the `toggleFeatureFlag` tRPC endpoint, it runs `isAuthed` and `isAdminMiddleware`. This is the backend security checkpoint that blocks non-admins by throwing an UNAUTHORIZED error(existing code).
* After Prisma updates the database and returns the row, `@Unmemoize` runs inside `CachedFeatureRepository.update` to explicitly delete the per-flag and all-flags cache keys in Redis (existing code).

3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?

* If the network request drops or the database update fails, it triggers SecurityView's onError callback to show a "Couldn't update..." toast and revert the switch. Left out because it is a standard infrastructure edge case.
* If Redis fails during the `@Unmemoize` step, the error is caught and logged internally by the decorator (try/catch and Promise.allSettled). Left out because the error is swallowed internally. Since the database save still succeeds and no error is returned to the frontend, the network replies remain the same, making it redundant. 

**Cross-cutting:**

4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."

I first proposed a text based outline of the feature's architecture and asked AI to create the Mermaid code for the diagrams. I then verifed the output agasint the actual codebase by analying the diagram that was created from the code and manually editing the diagram. Along the way, I asked AI to verify my edits. For example, I had to manually correct and add several details: adding conditional paths for user cancellations and non admin errros, correcting the updatedBy field to reflect the codebase, and fixing the cache clearing step to show that `@Unmemoize` runs inside `CachedFeatureRepository.update` method, not a standalone step.

+export type PartialDayOutOfOfficeWindow<T> = {
+  // Every host-zone calendar date the window touches, because the away map is keyed by date (slots.ts).

+export function getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows<T extends { start: Date; end: Date }>(
+  entries: T[],
+  timeZone: string
+): PartialDayOutOfOfficeWindow<T>[] {

+    .filter((entry) => !isWholeDayOutOfOffice(entry))
+    .map((entry) => {
+      const start = wallClockToTimeZone(entry.start, timeZone);
+      const end = wallClockToTimeZone(entry.end, timeZone);
+      // Step through the dates in UTC so a DST change in the host's zone cannot shift a day boundary.
+      const lastDate = end.format("YYYY-MM-DD");
+      const dates: string[] = [];
+      for (
+        let day = dayjs.utc(start.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));
+        day.format("YYYY-MM-DD") <= lastDate;
+        day = day.add(1, "day")
+      ) {
+        dates.push(day.format("YYYY-MM-DD"));
+      }
+      return { dates, start, end, entry };
+    });

# Sprint 2 mid-sprint check-in: zach-short

## What did you implement so far in the sprint, and what remains?

As of 2026-10-18, six days into Sprint 2, I have not written Sprint 2 code yet. My work so far is the D1 backlog. I carried my Sprint 1 issue #5 (event theme) into Sprint 2 and re-estimated it from `effort:high` to `effort:medium`, with the scope cut to colors and the image left out. I wrote and posted a new medium issue, #104, which shows the away badge and the redirect for out-of-office entries that cover only part of a day. It picks up a limit I named in my Sprint 1 PR #85. I also created the Sprint 2 milestone and attached both issues to it.

What remains is the build. For #5 and #104 I still need the D2 specs, peer-reviewed before I start coding, and the D3 design decisions with at least two alternatives each. After that come the pull requests with the new Tech Debt section, the AI logs in `ai-logs/sprint2/zach-short/`, and the D6 class and sequence diagrams for one of the two issues.

## What is one thing you learned about the codebase or about software engineering practice?

Code that reads a piece of data can carry assumptions about its shape that the data model does not show. Before PR #85, an out-of-office entry always covered whole days, and the booking page was written around that. `AvailableTimes.tsx` shows the "away" panel only when every slot of a day is away, or when only the first or only the last slot is (lines 266 to 293). `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx` says it outright in a comment, "since OOO is date-level, just check the first slot" (line 206).

PR #85 let an entry carry a leave time and a return time. The `start` and `end` columns were already `DateTime`, so the schema accepted the change without a migration, and the slot engine and its tests were correct. The booker was the part that was not ready: a window in the middle of a day fits neither of its cases. So PR #85 treats a partial-day entry as busy time with no badge, and the badge is now its own issue, #104.

## What is one thing you would do differently?

If I started issue #6 again, I would list every reader of the out-of-office data before I wrote the spec. The entries feed the per-day away map in `getUserAvailability.ts`, the slot builder in `slots.ts`, two booker components, the date picker, the entry list in settings and the API v2 slot output. My spec for #6 named only the schema, the create handler and the form as the parts to change, and it raised the redirect as an open question.

The badge limit came up during the build instead. It went into PR #85 as a known limit, with the alternatives written out in the Design section. By then it was a decision made late, inside a PR that already had 662 changed lines of code. With the readers listed first, the spec could have put the badge out of scope in plain words, or split it into its own issue from the start, and my reviewer would have seen that trade-off before any code existed.

# PR draft: issue #104 (away panel and redirect for partial-day out-of-office entries)

**Status: NOT OPENED.** Built 2026-10-26 in worktree `.claude/worktrees/issue-104`, branch
`feat/issue-104-partial-day-ooo-away` off `origin/main` at `a3e80d3d5a`, committed as `1b52360b42` and
pushed. Zach chose one PR. Open it as a **draft PR** (`agents/rules/quality-pr-creation.md`).

- **Title:** `feat: show the away panel for partial-day out-of-office entries (#104)`
- **Base:** `main`
- **Media:** four screenshots from the 2026-10-26 walk, uploaded to #110 through Claude in Chrome;
  the `user-attachments` URLs below are the ones on the PR.
- **Size:** 956 lines, 295 of them in code files and 661 in tests, 5 code files and 5 test files. Over
  the 500-line guideline in `AGENTS.md`; the Checklist line below says so.

Everything below the line is the PR body.

---

## What does this PR do?

- Closes #104

Since PR #85 a host can be away for part of a day. The booking page removed those slots and said nothing,
so an attendee saw a gap with no reason and no "Book with" link. A whole-day entry already shows the
"away" panel with the emoji, the reason, the public note and the redirect. This PR gives a partial-day
entry the same panel, in the place in the day where the window falls. This is "alternative 1" from the
PR #85 design.

**The slot engine.** A partial-day window now stays in the host's `dateRanges`, so its slots are generated
and then marked `away`, the same path a whole day takes. The window is still subtracted from
`oooExcludedDateRanges`, which is what `ensureAvailableUsers` checks a booking against, so an away slot
cannot be booked (criterion 2). The per-day away map (`IOutOfOfficeData`) keeps one record per date and
gains an optional `windows` list on it, each window carrying its UTC `start` and `end` and the entry's
data. A date without `windows` is away all day, as before. A whole-day entry wins over a window on the
same date, and a holiday replaces windows but not a whole-day entry. `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows`
in `date-ranges.ts` reads the stored wall-clock values with the DST-safe parse from PR #85 and lists every
host-zone date a window touches, so a window past midnight appears under both dates.

**Slot marking.** `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` marks a slot on a windowed date away only when the slot
overlaps a window: `slotStart < windowEnd && slotEnd > windowStart`. Any overlap counts (criterion 1), so
a slot that straddles the leave time is away too, which matches what the booking guard rejects. Whole-day
marking is unchanged. The windows are parsed to numbers once per `getSlots` call.

**The booker.** `AvailableTimes` renders one away panel at the first slot of each run of away slots and
hides the away slots, so the panel sits between the slots before and after the window (criterion 3). Two
windows on one day give two panels. The panel keeps today's text; no new string. The "Book with" button
already works from the slot's `toUser`, so the redirect needs only the data (criterion 4).
`AvailableTimeSlots` now hides the time-format toggle only when every slot of the day is away, not when
the first one is. `DatePicker`, `useNonEmptyScheduleDays` and the weekly view already require every slot
to be away before they treat a day as away, so a window that covers the whole working day renders as a
whole-day entry (criterion 5) and nothing else changes for them. API v2 slot responses filter `away` and
are unchanged (criterion 7).

**Decisions, from the issue's open questions.** Any overlap marks a slot away, because the fully-inside
rule would show slots the booking guard then rejects. The panel keeps today's text; its place between the
slots shows the window, and that is also the answer for attendees far from the host's zone. Two windows
give two panels. Criterion 4 stays, shown by a unit test; the redirect switch in the form is still
disabled in this fork, so a hand-edited `OutOfOfficeEntry.toUserId` row is the only way to see it live.

## Design

**Decision.** Keep the away map keyed by date and hang the windows under the date record. Whole days and
partial days then share one map, one lookup in the slot engine and one set of booker readers.

**Alternatives considered.**

1. A separate map of windows next to `datesOutOfOffice`. Every consumer of the map (the slot engine, the
   tRPC slots util, the onboarding hook) would take a second argument, and the whole-day-wins rule would
   live in two places.
2. One record per window with the date record replaced by a list. Every reader of
   `IOutOfOfficeData["anyDate"]` in the booker and the `DatePicker` would change shape for a feature that
   most days never use.
3. Mark only slots fully inside the window. A slot that straddles the leave time would look bookable and
   fail at booking time, a silent error.

**Rationale.** The windowed record is additive: a date without `windows` is exactly what it was before,
so existing tests pass unchanged (criterion 6), and the engine keeps the whole-day and partial-day split
that PR #85 introduced. Windows are read from the same `wallClockToTimeZone` parse, so the DST behaviour
is the one already tested.

**Consequences.** `SlotInfo` in `packages/features/calendars/lib/types.ts` still lists no `notes`, though
the server sends it and the panel shows it; the new booker test widens the type locally and the component
is left alone. `buildDateRanges` now skips windowed dates when it removes whole days from
`oooExcludedDateRanges`; without that line a windowed date lost all of its bookable ranges, which the
new tests caught.

{"assignees":["zach-short"],"comments":[],"labels":["enhancement","effort:medium"],"milestone":"Sprint 2","number":5,"state":"OPEN","title":"Ability to set event theme"}
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

<!--
  Provide a clear and concise description of what the problem is.
  For example, "I'm always frustrated when..."
-->

As a user, I want to have the ability to set my event to have a specific background and foreground color. It would also be nice to have the ability to set a background picture as a substitute for a color as well.

### Describe the solution you'd like

<!--
  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
-->
A setting leaflet underneath the layout leaflet that allows for setting a background/foreground color, as well as an image for the given event.



### User Story

As an event host, I want to set a background color and a text color for an event type's public booking page, so that each event looks the way I want when attendees book it.

### User Scenario

A host runs two events, "Design review" and "Coffee chat". For "Coffee chat" the host opens the event type, finds the new color setting under the layout setting, picks a warm background and a dark text color, and saves. The booking link for "Coffee chat" now shows those colors. "Design review" looks the same as before.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The event type editor has a background color setting and a text color setting under the layout setting. It is off by default.
2. When the setting is off or has never been set, the booking page looks exactly as it does today.
3. When colors are set, the public booking page for that event type shows the chosen background and text colors.
4. The colors apply to one event type only. Other event types of the same host are unchanged.
5. After saving and reloading the editor, the pickers show the saved values.
6. Only valid color values (hex) are accepted. An invalid value is rejected on save and shows an error.
7. If the text and background colors fail a contrast check, the editor shows a warning.

### Out of Scope

- A background image (named in the original request; deferred so this issue stays on colors).
- Gradients, fonts and other styling.
- Team-level or account-level themes.
- Colors in emails and calendar invites.

### Open Questions

- Does "event" mean the public booking page (assumed here) or the host's own dashboard views?
- One color pair, or separate light and dark theme values like the existing event type color?
- If the booking page's own light or dark theme conflicts with the chosen colors, which one wins?
- Should failing the contrast check only warn (assumed here), or block saving?
- Where do the values live: new columns, or the existing JSON? New columns need approval first, because the repo rules ask before schema changes.

### Technical Notes (from reading the code, to be confirmed while implementing)

- `EventType.eventTypeColor` already stores a light and a dark color (`packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts`) and has an "Event type color" toggle in the Advanced tab (`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx`). It only draws an accent stripe in the event types list, the bookings list and the bookings calendar view. It is not applied to the booking page. It is the closest existing pattern (storage, toggle, contrast warning text in the translations).
- The booking page takes brand colors from the user or team in `packages/features/bookings/Booker/utils/use-brand-colors.tsx`, a likely place to start for applying per-event colors.
- The planning doc scored this 4 points and assumed a schema change. The GitHub label says `effort:high`, which fits only if the image is included.

### Details (AI help in finding the bugs)

1. **Round-robin: one host's partial-day window hides slots other hosts could take.** This splits into two parts:
   - **New in this PR (risk; Confirmed in the running app through the slots API).**
     - Team slots come from each host's `oooExcludedDateRanges`, combined across hosts (`getAggregatedAvailability.ts:65`). If host A is away 14:00–16:00, the other hosts still offer those times. But `getSlots` marks slots using only the first host's away map (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots/util.ts:1098`).
     - With this PR, A's window is in that map (`getUserAvailability.ts:826-845`), so the slots are marked away (`slots.ts:14-25`). API v2 drops away slots (`slots-output.service.ts:49`; AC 7).
     - **How I tested it:** `slots/getSchedule` with `eventTypeId: 20` (`round-robin-seeded-team-event`, 5 hosts) on 2026-11-10.
       - With a 2:00–4:00pm entry for `teampro`, the 14:00 slot came back `"away": true` with `"fromUser": Team Pro Example`.
       - With the same entry on `teampro2` instead, no slot was away. A whole-day entry on `teampro2` had no effect either.
       - On `main`, with the same `teampro` entry, no slot was away. Partial-day entries never reach the map there, so the slots stay bookable. This confirms the change comes from this PR.
     - Team booking pages were removed in this fork (`ab21c7f805`), so no web booking page reaches this today. That's why it's a risk rather than a bug.
     - Suggestion: a test with two round-robin hosts, plus either skipping window marking for team events or a Tech Debt note.
   - **Pre-existing, not counted against this PR.** The same `[0]` map already marks every slot of a whole-day OOO date away for the whole round-robin team. That issue is separate from #104 (team events are out of scope there) and is worth its own issue.
2. **Window just after midnight (minor bug, rare; Confirmed in the running app).** Slots are looked up by the date of the slot's start (`slots.ts:220-227`), and a window is listed only under the dates it touches (`date-ranges.ts:256-277`). So a slot that starts before midnight and overlaps a window starting after midnight is shown as bookable, and `ensureAvailableUsers` then rejects it. That is the "looks bookable, then fails" case the any-overlap rule is meant to prevent.
   - **Reproduced** as `pro` (Europe/London): availability running across midnight from 11/10 into 11/11, the `30min` event set to 45 minutes, and an out-of-office entry on 11/11 from 12:00am to 9:00am.
   - The 11/10 11:45pm slot (ends 12:30am on 11/11) was offered as a normal time. Booking it failed with "Could not book the meeting. No available users found."
   - This only happens when working hours cross midnight. A possible fix: also list each window under the day before its start date, or check the date of the slot's end as well as its start.
3. **Unused helper (nit, Confirmed).** `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` (`date-ranges.ts:279`) has no production callers left, only tests (`date-ranges.test.ts:1297-1375`). Remove it, or keep the tests on `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows`.

```text
{"assignees":["zach-short"],"comments":[],"createdAt":"2026-10-18T22:06:45Z","labels":["enhancement","effort:medium"],"milestone":"Sprint 2","number":104,"state":"OPEN","title":"Show the away badge and redirect for partial-day out-of-office entries"}

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

PR #85 (closes #6) lets a host set a leave time and a return time on an out-of-office entry. The booking page now removes the slots inside that window, but it does that the way it removes a calendar event: the slots are gone, and nothing says why. A whole-day entry shows the "away" panel with the reason, the emoji, the public note and, when a redirect user is set, a "Book with <name>" button. A partial-day entry shows none of these. PR #85 names this as a known limit ("Partial-day entries do not show the "away" badge or a redirect on the booking page") and describes "alternative 1" as the path to fix it.

### Describe the solution you would like

Build alternative 1 from PR #85: teach the per-day out-of-office map about time ranges. Slots inside a partial-day window stay in the slot list, marked `away` with the entry's reason, emoji, note and redirect user, the same data a whole-day entry carries. The booker then renders one "away" panel at the place in the day where the window falls, between the slots before it and the slots after it. Away slots stay unbookable, as they are for whole days today.

### User Story

As an attendee who opens a host's booking page, I want to see that the host is away for part of the day, and book with their redirect user if one is set, so that I know why some times are missing and where to book instead.

### User Scenario

A host works 09:00 to 17:00 and has a partial-day entry from 14:00 to 16:00 with the reason "Doctor" and a public note. An attendee opens the booking page for that day. Slots from 09:00 run up to the slot that ends at 14:00. Below them is the away panel with the emoji, the reason and the note. Below the panel, slots resume at 16:00. If the entry has a redirect user, the panel also shows "Book with <name>", and the button opens that user's booking page on the same date.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. For a partial-day entry, every slot that overlaps the window is returned with `away: true` and the entry's `fromUser`, `toUser`, `reason`, `emoji`, and the note when `showNotePublicly` is on. Slots that do not overlap the window have no `away` flag.
2. A slot marked away for a partial-day entry cannot be booked. Booking it returns the same error as booking inside a whole-day entry.
3. On the booking page, a day with a partial-day window shows the bookable slots before the window, one away panel, and the bookable slots after the window, in that order. This holds when the window is at the start of the day, in the middle, or at the end.
4. When the entry has a redirect user, the away panel shows "Book with <name>", and clicking it opens that user's booking page on the same date, as it does for a whole-day entry.
5. A partial-day entry that covers all of the host's working hours on a day renders that day exactly as a whole-day entry does, in the time list and in the date picker.
6. Whole-day entries, holidays and calendar busy times render and block exactly as before. Existing tests for them pass unchanged.
7. API v2 slot responses do not change. Away slots stay filtered out of them (`slots-output.service.ts:49` and `:119` already do this).
8. Unit tests cover criteria 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6, including a window on a DST change day in America/New_York.

### Out of Scope

- Setting a redirect user from the out-of-office form. The redirect switch is disabled in this fork (`hasTeamPlan = false`, `CreateOrEditOutOfOfficeModal.tsx:190`, used at `:483`). This issue only renders a redirect that is already stored.
- Partial-day entries through API v2, which still stores whole days (PR #85, Known limits).
- Team and round-robin events. Their availability uses `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`getAggregatedAvailability.ts:43` and `:65`), so whole-day entries show no away panel there either.
- Changes to the out-of-office form or list from PR #85.

### Open Questions

- Which slots count as "inside" the window? A 30-minute event at 13:45 overlaps a 14:00 leave time. Criterion 1 says any overlap marks the slot away. The other option is to drop overlapping slots and mark only the slots fully inside the window. A window shorter than one slot interval (for example 14:10 to 14:20) may otherwise produce no away slot and so no panel.
- What does the panel say for a 2-hour entry? Today it says the host is away with no times. Should a partial-day panel show the leave and return times ("Away 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM")? That needs a new string in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` and the times in the attendee's timezone, not the host's.
- Two partial-day entries on one day (for example 10:00 to 11:00 and 14:00 to 15:00): two panels, or one? The per-day map holds one entry per date today, so this decides the shape of the data.
- Timezone edges. The map is keyed by the host's date (`slots.ts:189-192` formats the slot in `datesOutOfOfficeTimeZone`). An attendee several hours away can see a host's evening window on their next day. Is it enough that the panel sits between the right slots in the attendee's view, or must the panel also say the host's local times?
- The redirect cannot be set from the UI or from API v2 in this fork today. Is criterion 4 worth keeping if it can be shown only with a unit test and a hand-edited `OutOfOfficeEntry.toUserId` row?

### Technical Notes (from reading the code, to be confirmed while implementing)

Line numbers are from `origin/main` at `cc65a9670f`.

- **Where partial entries leave the map today.** `UserAvailabilityService.calculateOutOfOfficeRanges` returns early for any entry that fails `isWholeDayOutOfOffice` (`packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts:748`). The predicate is at `packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.ts:228`. The partial entries go to `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` instead (`date-ranges.ts:248`, called at `getUserAvailability.ts:482`).
- **Why the slots vanish.** The partial ranges are appended to the busy times (`getUserAvailability.ts:651-657`) and subtracted from both `dateRanges` and `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`:659-660`). A whole-day entry is different: it stays in `dateRanges`, so its slots are generated and then marked away, and it is removed only from `oooExcludedDateRanges` through `groupedOOO` (`date-ranges.ts:297-300` and `:354-361`). To get away slots, a partial window must follow the same split: subtract it from `oooExcludedDateRanges` only, and keep it in `dateRanges`.
- **Booking stays blocked.** `ensureAvailableUsers` checks a booking against `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/ensureAvailableUsers.ts:220`), so once the window is removed there, a booking inside it is still rejected. Criterion 2 needs a test for this.
- **Slot marking is date-level.** `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` looks up `datesOutOfOffice[YYYY-MM-DD]` and marks every slot on that date (`packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts:187-221`). It needs a time check for partial entries. `IOutOfOfficeData` (`getUserAvailability.ts:209`) maps a date to one entry, so the type must carry the window (for example optional `start` and `end`, or a list per date). See the open question on two entries in one day.
- **The booker assumes away means a whole day.** `AvailableTimes` shows the panel when every slot is away, or when only the first or only the last slot is away, and it hides every away slot (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.tsx:266-293`). A mid-day window has neither its first nor its last slot away, so no panel renders. It must render the panel at the first away slot of each run. `AvailableTimeSlots` decides that a day is away from its first slot only (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimeSlots.tsx:206`, comment "since OOO is date-level"), which hides the time-format toggle when a window starts the day.
- **The redirect.** The "Book with" button is in `OutOfOfficeInSlots.tsx`, which calls `router.push` to `/${toUser.username}` with the date. It already works from the slot data, so criterion 4 needs only the data in criterion 1.
- **Other readers of `away`.** `DatePicker.tsx:256-269` marks a day as away only when every slot is away, which gives criterion 5 for free. `useNonEmptyScheduleDays.ts:13` and the weekly view `Empty.tsx:66` also read the flag. Check that they do not change for a partial window.
- **Test that must change.** PR #85 added `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`, which asserts that a partial-day entry "stays off the away map". This issue reverses that on purpose. Update the case, do not delete it.
- **DST.** Keep the `wallClockToTimeZone` parse from PR #85 (`date-ranges.ts:241-246`) for the window edges. `.tz(zone, true)` returns the wrong offset near a DST change.

### Additional context

Estimate: medium (`effort:medium`). The likely files are `getUserAvailability.ts`, `date-ranges.ts`, `slots.ts`, `AvailableTimes.tsx`, `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx`, plus `slots.test.ts`, `date-ranges.test.ts`, `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`, and a new test for `AvailableTimes`. That is about 5 code files and 4 test files, under the 10-file limit in `AGENTS.md`. The slot engine part reuses a pattern that whole-day entries already use, which keeps it medium. The booker change is the part that could grow, because no unit test covers `AvailableTimes` today (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/` has tests only for `Booker`, `BookingDetailsSheet` and `DatePicker`). If the diff passes 500 lines, split it: engine and slots first, booker second.

function processOOO(outOfOffice: Dayjs, timeZone: string) {
  const OOOdate = outOfOffice.tz(timeZone, true);
  return {
    start: OOOdate,
    end: OOOdate,
  };
}

// The create handler strips the client's UTC offset before saving, so OutOfOfficeEntry.start and .end hold
// the host's wall-clock time in UTC columns. An entry saved as whole days spans 00:00:00.000 to 23:59:59.999.
export function isWholeDayOutOfOffice({ start, end }: { start: Date; end: Date }): boolean {
  return (
    start.getUTCHours() === 0 &&
    start.getUTCMinutes() === 0 &&
    start.getUTCSeconds() === 0 &&
    start.getUTCMilliseconds() === 0 &&
    end.getUTCHours() === 23 &&
    end.getUTCMinutes() === 59 &&
    end.getUTCSeconds() === 59 &&
    end.getUTCMilliseconds() === 999
  );
}

// `.tz(timeZone, true)` (keepLocalTime, which processOOO uses for midnight) resolves a wall-clock time that
// falls within a few hours of a DST change against the wrong offset: 03:30 on 2026-03-08 in America/New_York
// came back as 04:30-05:00. Parsing the wall-clock string in the zone returns 03:30-04:00.

# PR draft: issue #5 (booking page background and text colors per event type)

**Status: NOT OPENED.** Built 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-26 on branch `feat/issue-5-event-theme` off
`origin/main`, six commits ending at `5d9cba6431`, not pushed as of 2026-10-29. Open it as a **draft PR**
(`agents/rules/quality-pr-creation.md`).

- **Title:** `feat: set a booking page background and text color per event type (#5)`
- **Base:** `main`
- **Media:** none yet. The browser walk is still owed; the Image Demo section below has the two shots to
  take.
- **Size:** 633 lines (616 added, 17 removed) in 20 files: 238 lines in 14 code files, 378 in 6 test
  files, 12 in the generated OpenAPI file and 5 in the English locale. Over the 10-file guideline in
  `AGENTS.md`; the Checklist line below says so.

Everything below the line is the PR body.

---

## What does this PR do?

- Closes #5

A host can now give one event type its own background color and text color, and the public booking
page for that event type paints its booking card with them. Every other event type, and every event
type that never set the colors, looks exactly as it does today.

**The editor.** The Advanced tab's existing "Event type color" toggle gains two pickers, "Booking page
background color" and "Booking page text color", under the two accent pickers that were already there.
The pickers start at white and near-black but save nothing until the host changes one, so a saved event
type without booking page colors keeps the theme defaults (criteria 1 and 2). The values are stored in
the event type's existing `eventTypeColor` JSON next to the accent colors, as optional `backgroundColor`
and `textColor` keys, so there is no schema change and no migration. The stored schema now accepts only
`#rgb` or `#rrggbb` for the two new keys (criterion 6). A WCAG contrast check runs on every change and
shows the existing warning text when the pair fails it (criterion 7). The description string under the
toggle now says which colors bookers see.

**The booking page.** `getPublicEvent` selects `eventTypeColor`, parses it, and replaces it in the public
payload with `bookingPageColors`, which holds only the two booking page keys. The accent colors never
leave the server, which keeps the promise the editor makes about them. A malformed stored value becomes
`null` rather than an error, so one bad row cannot break a booking page. The booker maps the colors to
the theme's CSS variables (`--cal-bg`, `--cal-bg-muted`, `--cal-text`, `--cal-text-emphasis`, and the
subtle and muted text as a 70% mix of the text color) in an inline `style` on the booker wrapper, so the
colors render on the server with no flash and apply to the booking card only (criteria 3 and 4). After a
save and a reload the pickers read the saved values back (criterion 5).

**API v2.** `EventTypeColor_2024_06_14` gains optional, nullable `bookingPageBackgroundHex` and
`bookingPageTextHex`, documented in the OpenAPI spec. Create and update validate them with the same
hex rule as the stored schema and answer 400 on a bad value. Reads return them when set. On update, a
client that sends `color` with only the two accent fields keeps the stored booking page colors; sending
`null` clears one. Without that rule an API client that only knew the old shape would erase what the
host set in the editor.

## Design

**Decision 1: where the values live.** They go in the existing `eventTypeColor` JSON column as two
optional keys.

Alternatives considered:

1. Two new columns on `EventType`. Cleanest to query, but a schema change needs approval first in this
   repo, and the colors are only ever read together with the accent colors by the same screen.
2. The `metadata` JSON. It already carries layout settings, but it is parsed by a large shared schema
   with many readers, and a bad value there has a wider blast radius.
3. The existing `eventTypeColor` JSON (chosen). Same toggle, same save path, same reader, and rows saved
   before this change still parse because the new keys are optional.

Consequence: the public payload has to strip the accent colors by hand, which `withBookingPageColors`
does, and a stored value that fails the new hex rule makes the whole color object parse to `null`. That
is why the API validates before writing.

**Decision 2: how the booking page applies them.** An inline style of CSS variables on the booker
wrapper, scoped to the card.

Alternatives considered:

1. Extend `use-brand-colors`, which sets the user's brand color. It writes global CSS on the client after
   mount, so the page would flash the theme colors first, and it would color the whole page including the
   surrounding chrome.
2. A class per event type with generated CSS. Needs a build step or a style tag per event type, and the
   theme switch would fight it.
3. Inline CSS variables on the wrapper (chosen). Server rendered, no flash, and the variables stay inside
   the booker during client navigation to another event. Only the card changes, which was the owner's
   call.

Consequence: dark mode paints the container from `--cal-bg-muted`, so both background variables are set
to the same color, and secondary text is derived from the text color with `color-mix` so it stays
readable over any background.

**Decision 3: API v2 update semantics.** A field that is left out keeps the stored value; `null` clears
it. The alternative, treating a missing field as a clear, is what the accent colors do today, and it
would let any existing API client wipe the editor's colors on every update.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The two accent colors (`lightThemeHex`, `darkThemeHex`) in API v2 are still not
validated: `color` has `@Type` but no `@ValidateNested`, so the `@IsHexColor` rules on them never run.
This PR validates only the two new fields in the service and leaves the accent fields alone, because a
400 on a value the API accepts today would be a breaking change for existing clients
(`agents/rules/api-no-breaking-changes.md`). The hex regex is also written twice, once in
`packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts` and once in the platform input type, because the shared `isValidHexCode`
in `@calcom/lib/getBrandColours` pulls in `@calcom/embed-core` and cannot be imported from either place.

**Encountered:** The OpenAPI file on `main` had drifted from the generator in three unrelated places
(a Google Calendar description, the schedules description, and an `INSTANT_MEETING` webhook enum value).
The regeneration was run and only the `EventTypeColor_2024_06_14` hunk was kept, so this PR does not
carry the unrelated drift. `getTeamEventType.ts` shares `getPublicEventSelect` and so now also returns
the raw `eventTypeColor`; it has no caller in `apps/web` or `packages`, so it is left as is. The
`node:process`-style import reorders that Biome wanted in untouched files were reverted as not mine.

+import type { BookingPageColors } from "@calcom/features/eventtypes/lib/getBookingPageColors";
+import type { CSSProperties } from "react";
+
+// An inline style renders on the server, so the page never flashes the theme colors, and the
+// values stay inside this booker during client navigation to another event.
+export function getBookingPageColorStyle(colors: BookingPageColors | null | undefined): CSSProperties {
+  if (!colors) return {};
+
+  const { backgroundColor, textColor } = colors;
+  // The booker container paints from --cal-bg-muted in dark mode, so both must be set.
+  const backgroundVariables = backgroundColor
+    ? { "--cal-bg": backgroundColor, "--cal-bg-muted": backgroundColor }
+    : {};
+  const textVariables = textColor
+    ? {
+        "--cal-text": textColor,
+        "--cal-text-emphasis": textColor,
+        // Mixing with transparent keeps secondary text readable over any background color.
+        "--cal-text-subtle": `color-mix(in srgb, ${textColor} 70%, transparent)`,
+        "--cal-text-muted": `color-mix(in srgb, ${textColor} 70%, transparent)`,
+      }
+    : {};
+
+  return { ...backgroundVariables, ...textVariables } as CSSProperties;
+}
diff --git a/packages/features/eventtypes/lib/getBookingPageColors.ts b/packages/features/eventtypes/lib/getBookingPageColors.ts
new file mode 100644

+++ b/packages/features/eventtypes/lib/getBookingPageColors.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+import { eventTypeColor } from "@calcom/prisma/zod-utils";
+
+export type BookingPageColors = {
+  backgroundColor?: string;
+  textColor?: string;
+};
+
+export function getBookingPageColors(storedColors: unknown): BookingPageColors | null {
+  const parsed = eventTypeColor.safeParse(storedColors);
+  // One malformed row must never break a booking page, so it falls back to the theme colors.
+  if (!parsed.success || !parsed.data) return null;
+
+  const { backgroundColor, textColor } = parsed.data;
+  if (!backgroundColor && !textColor) return null;
+
+  return {
+    ...(backgroundColor ? { backgroundColor } : {}),
+    ...(textColor ? { textColor } : {}),
+  };
+}
+
+// The stored value also holds the accent colors, which the editor promises are never shown to
+// bookers, so the public payload carries only the booking page colors.
+export function withBookingPageColors<T extends { eventTypeColor: unknown }>(event: T) {
+  const { eventTypeColor: storedColors, ...eventWithoutStoredColors } = event;
+  return {
+    ...eventWithoutStoredColors,
+    bookingPageColors: getBookingPageColors(storedColors),
+  };
+}

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** `SlotInfo` in `packages/features/calendars/lib/types.ts` still has no `notes` field, though the server sends it and the away panel shows it. The new `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` widens the type locally instead of changing the shared type, to keep this PR on the slot engine and the panel. # PR draft: issue #5 (booking page background and text colors per event type)

**Status: NOT OPENED.** Built 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-26 on branch `feat/issue-5-event-theme` off
`origin/main`, six commits ending at `5d9cba6431`, not pushed as of 2026-10-29. Open it as a **draft PR**
(`agents/rules/quality-pr-creation.md`).

- **Title:** `feat: set a booking page background and text color per event type (#5)`
- **Base:** `main`
- **Media:** none yet. The browser walk is still owed; the Image Demo section below has the two shots to
  take.
- **Size:** 633 lines (616 added, 17 removed) in 20 files: 238 lines in 14 code files, 378 in 6 test
  files, 12 in the generated OpenAPI file and 5 in the English locale. Over the 10-file guideline in
  `AGENTS.md`; the Checklist line below says so.

Everything below the line is the PR body.

---

## What does this PR do?

- Closes #5

A host can now give one event type its own background color and text color, and the public booking
page for that event type paints its booking card with them. Every other event type, and every event
type that never set the colors, looks exactly as it does today.

**The editor.** The Advanced tab's existing "Event type color" toggle gains two pickers, "Booking page
background color" and "Booking page text color", under the two accent pickers that were already there.
The pickers start at white and near-black but save nothing until the host changes one, so a saved event
type without booking page colors keeps the theme defaults (criteria 1 and 2). The values are stored in
the event type's existing `eventTypeColor` JSON next to the accent colors, as optional `backgroundColor`
and `textColor` keys, so there is no schema change and no migration. The stored schema now accepts only
`#rgb` or `#rrggbb` for the two new keys (criterion 6). A WCAG contrast check runs on every change and
shows the existing warning text when the pair fails it (criterion 7). The description string under the
toggle now says which colors bookers see.

**The booking page.** `getPublicEvent` selects `eventTypeColor`, parses it, and replaces it in the public
payload with `bookingPageColors`, which holds only the two booking page keys. The accent colors never
leave the server, which keeps the promise the editor makes about them. A malformed stored value becomes
`null` rather than an error, so one bad row cannot break a booking page. The booker maps the colors to
the theme's CSS variables (`--cal-bg`, `--cal-bg-muted`, `--cal-text`, `--cal-text-emphasis`, and the
subtle and muted text as a 70% mix of the text color) in an inline `style` on the booker wrapper, so the
colors render on the server with no flash and apply to the booking card only (criteria 3 and 4). After a
save and a reload the pickers read the saved values back (criterion 5).

**API v2.** `EventTypeColor_2024_06_14` gains optional, nullable `bookingPageBackgroundHex` and
`bookingPageTextHex`, documented in the OpenAPI spec. Create and update validate them with the same
hex rule as the stored schema and answer 400 on a bad value. Reads return them when set. On update, a
client that sends `color` with only the two accent fields keeps the stored booking page colors; sending
`null` clears one. Without that rule an API client that only knew the old shape would erase what the
host set in the editor.

## Design

**Decision 1: where the values live.** They go in the existing `eventTypeColor` JSON column as two
optional keys.

Alternatives considered:

1. Two new columns on `EventType`. Cleanest to query, but a schema change needs approval first in this

```text
1. Two new columns on `EventType`. Cleanest to query, but a schema change needs approval first in this
   repo, and the colors are only ever read together with the accent colors by the same screen.
2. The `metadata` JSON. It already carries layout settings, but it is parsed by a large shared schema
   with many readers, and a bad value there has a wider blast radius.
3. The existing `eventTypeColor` JSON (chosen). Same toggle, same save path, same reader, and rows saved
   before this change still parse because the new keys are optional.

Consequence: the public payload has to strip the accent colors by hand, which `withBookingPageColors`
does, and a stored value that fails the new hex rule makes the whole color object parse to `null`. That
is why the API validates before writing.

**Decision 2: how the booking page applies them.** An inline style of CSS variables on the booker
wrapper, scoped to the card.

Alternatives considered:

1. Extend `use-brand-colors`, which sets the user's brand color. It writes global CSS on the client after
   mount, so the page would flash the theme colors first, and it would color the whole page including the
   surrounding chrome.
2. A class per event type with generated CSS. Needs a build step or a style tag per event type, and the
   theme switch would fight it.
3. Inline CSS variables on the wrapper (chosen). Server rendered, no flash, and the variables stay inside
   the booker during client navigation to another event. Only the card changes, which was the owner's
   call.

Consequence: dark mode paints the container from `--cal-bg-muted`, so both background variables are set
to the same color, and secondary text is derived from the text color with `color-mix` so it stays
readable over any background.

**Decision 3: API v2 update semantics.** A field that is left out keeps the stored value; `null` clears
it. The alternative, treating a missing field as a clear, is what the accent colors do today, and it
would let any existing API client wipe the editor's colors on every update.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The two accent colors (`lightThemeHex`, `darkThemeHex`) in API v2 are still not
validated: `color` has `@Type` but no `@ValidateNested`, so the `@IsHexColor` rules on them never run.
This PR validates only the two new fields in the service and leaves the accent fields alone, because a
400 on a value the API accepts today would be a breaking change for existing clients
(`agents/rules/api-no-breaking-changes.md`). The hex regex is also written twice, once in
`packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts` and once in the platform input type, because the shared `isValidHexCode`
in `@calcom/lib/getBrandColours` pulls in `@calcom/embed-core` and cannot be imported from either place.

**Encountered:** The OpenAPI file on `main` had drifted from the generator in three unrelated places
(a Google Calendar description, the schedules description, and an `INSTANT_MEETING` webhook enum value).
The regeneration was run and only the `EventTypeColor_2024_06_14` hunk was kept, so this PR does not
carry the unrelated drift. `getTeamEventType.ts` shares `getPublicEventSelect` and so now also returns
the raw `eventTypeColor`; it has no caller in `apps/web` or `packages`, so it is left as is. The
`node:process`-style import reorders that Biome wanted in untouched files were reverted as not mine.

## What does this PR do?

<!-- Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed. Please also include relevant motivation and context. List any dependencies that are required for this change.

Note: Cal.diy is a community-maintained open-source project. Contributions here do NOT flow to Cal.com's production service. -->
- This PR closes issue #11 

-This PR restores the frontend UI for Issue #11, which requires a reason when a booking is rescheduled based on the Event Type configuration.

It adds the "Require reschedule reason" setting to the Event Type Advanced settings and connects it to the existing reschedule reason requirement logic. When a reason is required, the reschedule dialog prevents submission until a reason is provided.

This PR also changes the default reschedule reason requirement to `OPTIONAL_BOTH` so existing event types do not unexpectedly begin requiring reschedule reasons.


## Visual Demo (For contributors especially)

A visual demonstration is strongly recommended, for both the original and new change **(video / image - any one)**.

#### Video Demo (if applicable):

- Show screen recordings of the issue or feature.
- Demonstrate how to reproduce the issue, the behavior before and after the change.

#### Image Demo (if applicable):

- Add side-by-side screenshots of the original and updated change.
- Highlight any significant change(s).
- 
<img width="500" height="355" alt="Screenshot 2026-09-21 212321" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a968f3ca-e30b-4da5-ba3b-0338c410d1d4" />
<img width="500" height="355" alt="Screenshot 2026-09-21 212437" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/45e936b9-1136-413f-8dd3-6930e236b6a6" />

## Technical Debt

**Introduced:**
- No known technical debt was introduced by this PR.

**Encountered:**
- The Event Type form was not initializing `requiresRescheduleReason` correctly, which caused an incorrect unsaved-changes warning when navigating away from the Advanced tab.
- Fixed this by including `requiresRescheduleReason` in the form's default values and adding automated tests to verify the behavior.
- Resolved the merge conflict in `EventAdvancedTab.tsx` while preserving the existing reminder email functionality.

**Remaining:**
- No known outstanding technical debt related to this PR.

## Mandatory Tasks (DO NOT REMOVE)

- [x] I have self-reviewed the code (A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected).
- [x] I have updated the developer docs if this PR makes changes that would require a documentation change. If N/A, write N/A here and check the checkbox.
- [x] I confirm automated tests are in place that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.



## How should this be tested?

### Manual Testing

1. Open an Event Type and navigate to the Advanced tab. Verify the **Require reschedule reason** dropdown appears.

2. Select **Mandatory for both**, save, and refresh. Verify the selected value persists.

3. Open the attendee reschedule dialog. Confirm **Request reschedule** is disabled when the reason is empty and enabled after entering a reason.

4. Change the setting to **Optional for both**, save, and refresh. Verify the dialog displays "(Optional)" and allows submission without a reason.

5. Navigate away from the Advanced tab without making changes. Confirm no incorrect unsaved-changes warning appears.

6. Change the reminder email dropdown, save, and refresh. Verify its value persists.

**Result: All six manual tests passed.**

### Automated Testing

- 10 RescheduleDialog tests passed.
- 3 EventAdvancedTab tests passed.
- 4 additional useEventTypeForm tests passed.
- 96 related tests passed.
- Type checks and Biome checks passed.


## Design decision
Issue #11 requested the same four values and default behavior as the cancellation reason setting, which uses MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY.

I chose OPTIONAL_BOTH as the default instead because existing event types should not unexpectedly require a reason when someone reschedules a booking. This keeps the feature backward-compatible while allowing organizers to choose a mandatory setting when needed.

Alternative considered: Using MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY to match the cancellation reason default. I decided against this because it would introduce a new requirement for existing event types.

# Review of PR #81 (issue #11)

Review state to select on GitHub: **Request changes**. Post the text under "Review text" as the review body. The rubric scores are proposals; Zach sets them.

PR: https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/81, head `1d61ffc112`, author `julissaehp`. Issue #11 was written by `zach-short`. The backend for #11 merged as #36 (`35d7f6c3bd`, 2026-09-18).

Evidence behind each point, gathered 2026-10-08:
- The edited migration is on `main` since #36 (`git log origin/main -- packages/prisma/migrations/20260916120000_add_reschedule_reason_require`).
- PostgreSQL fills existing rows with the default given in `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT`, and a later `SET DEFAULT` changes only new rows: shown on the local Postgres 14.18 with a temporary table, rows 1 and 2 kept `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` and row 3 got `OPTIONAL_BOTH`.
- Nothing on `main` can set `requiresRescheduleReason`: #36 added no UI, and `git grep` finds it in no file under `apps/api`, `packages/platform` or `docs`.
- The server already enforces the requirement: `requestReschedule.handler.ts:84` on `main`.
- CI on `1d61ffc112`: lint, type checks, unit and API v2 unit tests pass. `Check Prisma Migrations` fails in 2 seconds with "The template is not valid" in `check-prisma-migrations.yml` lines 16 and 17, and it fails the same way on #77, which merged. `Security Audit` fails on third-party advisories, as on every PR merged today.
- The only conflict with `main` (`fcb923e3cd`) is `EventAdvancedTab.tsx` (`git merge-tree`).

## Review text

### Summary

This PR adds the "Require reschedule reason" dropdown to Event Type, Advanced, next to the cancellation one. It passes the setting to the Request Reschedule dialog, which hides "(Optional)" and disables "Request reschedule" while a required reason is empty. It also changes the default from `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` to `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, in `schema.prisma`, in the existing migration and in `isRescheduleReasonRequired`.

The UI side looks right. The dialog uses the same `isRescheduleReasonRequired` helper as `requestReschedule.handler.ts:84`, so the button and the server agree. The repository select, the bookings query and the update schema all carry the new field. On `1d61ffc112`, lint, type checks and both unit test jobs pass in CI. The two red checks are not caused by this PR: `Check Prisma Migrations` fails because its workflow file is invalid (it fails the same way on #77), and `Security Audit` fails on third-party dependencies.

### Changes requested

#### 1. Do not edit a migration that is already on main

`20260916120000_add_reschedule_reason_require/migration.sql` merged with #36. A database that already ran it does not run it again, so this edit changes nothing there. The column keeps `DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY'`. Also, when that migration added the column, PostgreSQL filled every existing event type with `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`, not with NULL. So the new `?? OPTIONAL_BOTH` fallback never reaches those rows, and their hosts still must give a reason. That is the case this PR wants to prevent.

Please put the old migration back as it is on `main`, and add a new migration:

```sql
ALTER TABLE "EventType" ALTER COLUMN "requiresRescheduleReason" SET DEFAULT 'OPTIONAL_BOTH';
UPDATE "EventType" SET "requiresRescheduleReason" = 'OPTIONAL_BOTH' WHERE "requiresRescheduleReason" = 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY';
```

The `UPDATE` is safe now because nothing on `main` lets a host set this value, so every stored value came from the old default. After this PR merges, that is no longer true.

#### 2. Say why the default differs from #11

#11 asks for "the same four values and the same default posture" as the cancellation setting, and that default is `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`. `OPTIONAL_BOTH` is a reasonable choice, so existing event types do not change behavior. Please put that decision in the PR description with the alternative you did not take.

#### 3. Resolve the conflict and link the issue

The branch conflicts with `main` in `EventAdvancedTab.tsx`. The description also needs `Closes #11`, which the Sprint 1 spec asks for.

#### 4. Add tests and the test strategy

The only test change flips the expectation of one existing test. Please add tests for the new behavior: the dialog disables "Request reschedule" when a reason is required and the text is empty, enables it when there is text, and shows "(Optional)" only when no reason is required. A test that the Advanced tab saves the chosen value would also help. "How should this be tested?" still has the template prompts. Please replace them with the steps you used to check it.

### Minor

- The Checklist still has the template lines, for example the one that says the contributing guide was not read, and "My PR is too large". The template says to remove the lines that do not apply. As they are, they read as statements about this PR.
- `RescheduleDialog.tsx` moves the React imports, and `EventAdvancedTab.tsx` rewraps the cancellation `defaultValue`. If Biome made these changes, they are OK.

### Rubric

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness: does the change do what the issue asked? | 5 | The dropdown and the dialog work with the existing server check. The default change does not reach any database that already ran the #36 migration, and the branch conflicts with `main`. |
| Test coverage: are tests present and meaningful? | 4 | One existing test is updated for the new default. The dialog and the setting have no tests. |
| Code quality: consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | 7 | It follows the cancellation setting closely and reuses `isRescheduleReasonRequired`. Some formatting changes are unrelated. |
| Documentation: inline comments and PR description are clear | 4 | The description says what and why. The test section is the template, the checklist has template lines, and there is no `Closes #11`. |
| AI transparency: if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | 5 | Neither the PR nor #11 says whether AI was used. If it was, please link the log in a comment on #11. If not, one line there is enough. |
| Overall: would you merge this as-is? | 4 | Not as-is. After items 1, 3 and 4, yes. |

import { RescheduleReasonRequirement } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";

export function isRescheduleReasonRequired(
  setting: RescheduleReasonRequirement | null | undefined,
  isHost: boolean
): boolean {
  const requirement = setting ?? RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY;

  switch (requirement) {
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH:
      return false;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH:
      return true;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY:
      return isHost;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY:
      return !isHost;
    default:
      return false;
  }
}

## Sprint 1 carryovers and what changed

Issue #5 (event theme) was in the Sprint 1 milestone, assigned to me and labelled `effort:high`, and it was not started in Sprint 1, because I spent the sprint on #6 and #9 (PRs #85 and #78, both merged 2026-10-09) [Zach confirms]. On 2026-10-18 I moved it to the Sprint 2 milestone and changed the label to `effort:medium`. The scope changed with the label: the original request asked for a background color, a text color and a background image, and the image is now listed under Out of Scope in the issue body, so the issue covers the two colors only. My second Sprint 2 issue, #104, is new, but it continues Sprint 1 work: PR #85 let an out-of-office entry carry a leave time and a return time, and it named as a known limit that a partial-day entry shows no away panel and no redirect on the booking page. #104 builds "alternative 1" from the PR #85 design section to close that limit.

## Requirements and design: Zach's paragraph

Both specs are in the issue bodies: user story, user scenario, acceptance criteria (7 for #5, 8 for #104), Out of Scope, Open Questions, and technical notes with file and line references from reading the code. For #104 I answered the five open questions on 2026-10-26, before any code was written: any slot that overlaps the window is away (a fully-inside rule would show slots that the booking guard then rejects), the panel keeps today's text and its place between the slots shows the window, two windows on one day give two panels, and the redirect criterion stays, shown by a unit test and a hand-edited `toUserId` row. The design in PR #110 keeps the per-day away map keyed by date and adds an optional `windows` list to each date record, so a date without `windows` behaves exactly as before; it lists three rejected alternatives (a separate map of windows, one record per window, and marking only slots fully inside the window). For #5 the design in the PR body has three decisions with alternatives: the colors go in the existing `eventTypeColor` JSON as two optional keys (not new columns, which need schema approval, and not `metadata`); the booking page applies them as inline CSS variables on the booker wrapper, so they render on the server with no flash and color the booking card only (not through `use-brand-colors`, which writes global CSS after mount); and in API v2 a color field that is left out keeps the stored value while `null` clears it, so an existing API client cannot erase the colors set in the editor. Class and sequence diagrams for #104 (D6) are at `docs/sprint2/diagrams/104-zach-short.md`. Whether the two specs got a teammate's review before coding started: [verify].

## Test strategy: Zach's paragraph

Each feature has unit tests on the logic and a browser walk against the local dev server with the seed data. #110 changes five test files: `date-ranges.test.ts` (the windows helper, a window past midnight, two windows on the 2026-03-08 DST change in America/New_York), `slots.test.ts` (windows at the start, middle and end of a day, a slot that straddles the leave time, a window shorter than a slot, a window that covers the working day), `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts` (the away map and the slots a booker gets, also run under `VITEST_MODE=timezone`), `ensureAvailableUsers.outOfOffice.test.ts` (a booking inside the window or across the leave time is refused with the same error as a whole-day entry), and a new `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` (panel order, two panels, the redirect button). On 2026-10-26 the five files gave 129 passed and 2 skipped; the full unit suite gave 4338 passed and 1 failed, a Google Calendar timing benchmark that passes alone; the timezone project gave 68 passed and 2 skipped. Four of the new tests caught a silent bug in my first pass (a windowed date lost all of its bookable ranges) before any gate did. The walk on 2026-10-26 covered criteria 1, 3, 4 and 5, with four screenshots on #110. Criterion 2 (booking inside the window is refused) is covered by the unit test only, because the local database schema is behind the branch and `POST /api/book/event` fails there for every slot. #5 adds 32 unit tests: 8 for `getBookingPageColors`, 4 for `getBookingPageColorStyle`, 8 and 4 in the two API v2 transformer specs, and 8 for the hex check in `input-event-types.service.spec.ts`; the API v2 e2e spec gains the two fields in its create and update bodies, but the e2e suite was not run. Claude Code read the existing code and wrote the technical notes in both issue drafts, proposed options for each open question, wrote the code and tests once I chose the options, ran the gates, and drafted the PR bodies. For #104 it also walked the feature in a browser through Claude in Chrome and uploaded the screenshots to #110. [Zach confirms] I made the product decisions before any code was written (the overlap rule, the panel text and the redirect criterion for #104; card only, the locale change and the API v2 update rule for #5), and I read each diff before I committed it. [Zach confirms] Suggestions I rejected or narrowed: Biome's import reorders and a `node:process` import in files the change does not own were reverted; the OpenAPI regeneration for #5 also rewrote three unrelated parts of the spec, and only the `EventTypeColor_2024_06_14` hunk was kept; and I chose not to add hex validation to the existing API v2 accent colors, because a 400 on input the API accepts today would be a breaking change.

## Risks and retrospective: Zach's bullets

What went well:
- Writing file and line references into the #104 issue before building paid off: the PR touched the five code files the issue predicted, plus their tests.
- Answering the open questions in one batch before code kept the #104 build to one session on 2026-10-26, from worktree to pushed draft PR.
- The new tests caught the one silent failure in #104 before any gate or reviewer did.

What slowed me down:
- The #5 work started on my personal branch `short`, which was 134 commits behind `main` on 2026-10-19, so it had to be moved to `feat/issue-5-event-theme` before it could become a PR.
- The machine ran out of memory under `yarn dev` and the full gates. The #5 browser walk failed three times on 2026-10-19 and is still owed.
- The local `calendso` database schema is behind `schema.prisma`, so the booking handler cannot run here and one #104 criterion could be checked by unit test only.

What I would do differently:
- Branch from `origin/main` with the `feat/issue-<n>-<slug>` name on the first commit, and push early, so the work is visible to the team and reviewable before the due date.
- Put the course's required Tech Debt section in the PR body when the PR is opened; the #110 review noted it was missing.
- Ask for a teammate review as soon as the draft PR is up; the #110 review came on the due date, 2026-10-29.

Risks carried into Sprint 3:
- #110 review findings still open: a round-robin event can mark slots away from the first host's partial-day window (reachable through the slots API and API v2 only, since team booking pages were removed in this fork), and a slot that starts before midnight and overlaps a window after midnight looks bookable and is then refused.
- Both PRs are over the size guideline, which makes review slower.

import http.server, os, re, sys
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def __init__(self, *a, **k): super().__init__(*a, directory=ROOT, **k)
    def do_POST(self):
        name = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]', '', self.path.split('name=')[-1])
        n = int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0))
        data = self.rfile.read(n)
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'out', name), 'wb') as f: f.write(data)
        self.send_response(200); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b'ok')
os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, 'out'), exist_ok=True)
http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 8765), H).serve_forever()
EOF
